source_name: Здружение на информатичко-комуникациски технологии при Стопанска комора на СМ
why_relevant: The chamber's own ICT association (distinct from MASIT), with a governing board and elective sessions (a leadership election was held 7 October 2025). Participates in national ICT strategy work — a second, partly overlapping roster of ICT/payment-technology firms and a lobbying channel.

source_name: Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија (Macedonian e-Commerce Association) — ecommerce.mk
why_relevant: Described as the first and only e-commerce association in the country; publishes consumer-facing and merchant-facing content directly on payment-method preference ('Кој платежен систем го преферираат Македонците?'), online fraud, and e-payment onboarding for merchants across CEFTA markets. One of the few association sources producing quantitative claims about card vs cash-on-delivery behaviour.

source_name: Организација на потрошувачите на Македонија (ОПМ) — Consumer Organisation of Macedonia
why_relevant: National consumer body with a complaints intake (Пријави проблем / Внеси поплака), an advisory bureau, and an alternative dispute resolution track. It intervenes with inspectorates and regulators and pursues collective legal action when several consumers report the same trader — so it aggregates grievance signal about bank fees, ATM charges and card disputes that never appears in official statistics. Publishes a financial-services negotiation handbook.

source_name: Регистар на организации на потрошувачи (nvosorabotka.gov.mk) + Министерство за економија и труд consumer-protection pages
why_relevant: State-maintained listing of registered consumer organisations — the authoritative way to enumerate consumer bodies beyond ОПМ (regional/local ones) rather than guessing at them. The ministry's consumer-protection section documents the institutional framework and which body handles which grievance type.

source_name: AmCham North Macedonia — American Chamber of Commerce
why_relevant: Publishes formal position papers (a Digitalization Position Paper is hosted on the site) and an annual report, and its membership includes payments infrastructure firms — CaSys (International Card Systems AD Skopje), which serves banks and payment institutions in card operations, e-commerce and digital payment channels, is announced as a member. Position papers state industry asks on digital payments that official statistics never carry.

source_name: Совет на странски инвеститори / Foreign Investors Council (fic.mk) — White Book
why_relevant: Operates in association with the Economic Chamber and publishes a 'White Book' of investor grievances and reform asks covering the financial system, taxation and customs; a members catalogue also exists. White Books are a dense source of stated friction points on payments, banking and fiscal rules.

source_name: Сојуз на стопански комори на Македонија (Union of Chambers of Commerce, chamber.mk)
why_relevant: Second national chamber umbrella (independent, non-governmental) describing itself as connecting thousands of member companies with 1000+ national and international institutions. A parallel membership population and a distinct lobbying voice from mchamber.mk — needed so the merchant/SME population is not under-counted.

source_name: Стопанска комора на северо-западна Македонија / Oda Ekonomike e Maqedonisë Veriperëndimore (OEMVP)
why_relevant: Regional chamber for north-western North Macedonia, bilingual mk/sq, with a large Albanian-language SME and retail membership that the Skopje-centric chambers under-represent. Important for merchant-side cash-vs-card friction in Tetovo/Gostivar/Struga, and the only route into Albanian-language business advocacy in this cell.

source_name: Бизнис конфедерација на Северна Македонија / Business Confederation of North Macedonia (BCM)
why_relevant: Employers' confederation (organisation of employers), a social-partner voice distinct from the chambers, active in UN Global Compact since 2015. Employer-side positions on cash payments, wage payment channels and informal economy intersect directly with cash-usage questions.

source_name: Македонско-бугарска стопанска комора — Здружение за угостителство, хотелиерство и туризам
why_relevant: One of the few explicitly named hospitality/HORECA association pages found in local language; HORECA is the highest-cash-intensity acceptance segment and a standing complainant on card acceptance fees. Serves as an entry pointer into the hospitality actor set while a dedicated national HORECA association remains unlocated.

source_name: Стопанска комора — Годишни извештаи за активностите (annual activity reports, incl. archive subdomain)
why_relevant: The chamber publishes annual activity reports as PDFs (2010, 2020, 2022 editions observed) plus draft-law commentary PDFs. These enumerate which associations and groups were active, what regulatory files they worked on, and sometimes carry membership counts — a durable time series of the association landscape itself, and an archive subdomain (arhiva.mchamber.mk) preserves older ones.

source_name: Bankarstvo.mk — sector trade portal carrying association and financial-company positions
why_relevant: Specialist banking portal that reports association-level statements verbatim — e.g. financial companies' openness to fintech development, and a report on mass failures of payment cards, POS devices and ATMs in the country. Useful as a discovery layer for association statements that never get a page on the association's own site.

source_name: МБА LinkedIn / association social channels (MBA, MASIT, BCM, ОПМ Facebook)
why_relevant: Several of these bodies post statements and event outputs to social channels before or instead of their websites; ОПМ in particular is highly active on Facebook. Useful as a change-detection tripwire on association activity, not as a primary record.

source_name: Kapital.mk — business weekly / portal (КАПИТАЛ)
why_relevant: Leading MK business publication; tag-per-company architecture (e.g. /tag/komerczijalna-banka/) makes per-bank longitudinal tracking easy. Covers bank results, executive statements, M&A, tender outcomes and fee/pricing changes.

source_name: Faktor.mk — economy/business news portal
why_relevant: High-volume MK business portal that routinely re-reports and interprets NBRM payment-system releases (e-banking/mobile-banking user counts, cashless payment growth) and covers bank fees, card usage and ATM networks.

source_name: Pari.com.mk — financial/business portal
why_relevant: Publishes quantified cash-vs-card analyses (e.g. ATM withdrawals vs card transaction value in EUR, annual card transaction counts) — exactly the cash-usage / card-statistics angle of this run, often derived from NBRM data but with journalist framing and comparisons not in the official release.

source_name: MIA — Media Information Agency (state news agency)
why_relevant: National wire service; carries NBRM quarterly payment/digital-channel releases verbatim and early, and is the upstream text most other MK portals republish. Useful as the canonical timestamp for when a statistic entered public circulation. Also publishes in Albanian and English.

source_name: Sloboden Pečat — daily newspaper / portal, economy section
why_relevant: Major MK daily with a dedicated economy vertical; covers bank fees, consumer complaints, macro/monetary commentary and analyst opinion pieces on the domestic economy that provide context and named sources for payments topics.

source_name: Nezavisen Vesnik (nezavisen.mk)
why_relevant: Daily newspaper covering NBRM decisions with a consumer-cost framing (e.g. reporting that all banks adopted new tariffs with significantly reduced payment-order fees) — a pricing signal directly relevant to payments-market monitoring.

source_name: Fokus (fokus.mk) — weekly investigative newspaper
why_relevant: Investigative weekly; the natural venue for tender disputes, procurement irregularities and bank-supervision controversies that never appear in statistics. Named in the cell brief; existence confirmed via reference sources, but no banking/payments article was surfaced in this pass — treat as unverified for topical yield.

source_name: Makfax — news agency, economy section
why_relevant: Independent MK news agency with a consistently used economy vertical; carries NBRM Council sessions, macroeconomic projections, banking-system stability and digital-payment-channel releases. Reliable, structured, easy to crawl.

source_name: Denar.mk — economy/finance portal
why_relevant: Consumer-finance oriented portal running cash-preference stories („Ќе платам во кеш“) with quantified ATM-withdrawal vs POS-spend comparisons — direct cash-usage and ATM/POS signal in MK language.

source_name: Ekonomski.mk — economy news vertical
why_relevant: Economy-focused MK portal covering banking digitalisation, the new Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems, and new market entrants (PSPs/EMIs) — useful for tracking competitive structure of the MK payments market.

source_name: Telma TV — „Бизнис Објектив“ business programme
why_relevant: National broadcaster whose business show produces cash-vs-card segments and interviews with bankers/NBRM officials; broadcast statements are often the earliest public source for executive positions on ATM networks and merchant acceptance.

source_name: Alfa TV portal (alfa.mk) — economy
why_relevant: Broadcaster portal that republishes NBRM quarterly payment-statistics releases in full; useful as a redundancy/mirror channel when the primary NBRM page is unreachable, and for measuring how widely a statistic diffuses.

source_name: Kurir.mk — economy section
why_relevant: High-traffic portal mirroring NBRM payment/digital-channel releases; low originality but adds breadth for diffusion tracking and occasionally adds local reaction quotes.

source_name: Večer (vecer.mk) — economy section
why_relevant: Long-running MK daily with a stable economy category URL; adds historical depth for longitudinal media monitoring of banking/payments topics.

source_name: Nova Makedonija (novamakedonija.com.mk)
why_relevant: Oldest MK daily; economy coverage includes money-supply/M3 and banking-stability reporting citing NBRM, plus opinion/analysis columns naming domestic economists useful as an expert-actor map.
